guarantees.claim: The u_kmac_core instance drives msgfifo_ready, msg_valid, msg_data, msg_strb, kmac2sha3_process, kmac_core_state_error, and key_index_error directly from its output ports.

assumptions.claim: The handshake inputs (msgfifo_valid, msg_ready) follow a valid/ready protocol as expected by kmac_core; data and strb are stable when valid is asserted.
assumptions.risk: Protocol violation could cause data corruption, stall, or unintended message processing.

assumptions.claim: The key interface (key_data, key_len, key_valid) must deliver a correct key according to KMAC specification before or during the start of processing.
assumptions.risk: Invalid key material may lead to weak or incorrect MAC, breaking security guarantees.

assumptions.claim: Configuration inputs (app_kmac_en, app_sha3_mode, app_keccak_strength) are stable and legal during operation; kmac_en must properly gate operation.
assumptions.cond: after reset and during enabled periods
assumptions.risk: Illegal mode changes or inconsistent configuration could cause kmac_core to produce wrong hash or state machine errors.

assumptions.claim: lc_escalate_en[1] is assumed to be properly asserted by the life-cycle controller to disable kmac on security escalation; kmac_core only uses this single bit.
assumptions.cond: when a life-cycle escalation event occurs on this bit
assumptions.risk: If escalation signals on other bits are required, kmac_core will not be halted, allowing continued secret processing in a compromised state.

uncertain_points.claim: Only bit 1 of the lc_escalate_en vector is connected; other life-cycle escalation sources (e.g., bits 0,2,...) are ignored by kmac_core.
uncertain_points.risk: A non-bit-1 escalation would leave kmac_core operational, potentially exposing secret key material or ongoing MAC computation.
